title: Cream of Tomato Soup
description: Cream of Tomato Soup is a smooth, velvety soup made with tomatoes, mirepoix, stock, and finished with milk and fresh cream. It is a classic soup with a rich flavor and silky texture, commonly served as an appetizer.

ingredients.title: Base
items: Mirepoix – 80 g (finely chopped onions, carrots, and celery in 2:1:1 ratio)

ingredients.title: Flavoring & Seasoning
items: Bouquet garni – 1 bundle (thyme, bay leaf, parsley stems)
Ham or bacon skin – 1 small piece (optional, for extra depth)
Freshly ground black pepper – to taste

ingredients.title: Finishing & Garnish
items: Fresh parsley – a few sprigs, chopped (for garnish)
Bread croutons – as required (toasted or fried)

instruction.title: Step 1 – Preparing the Base
steps: Heat the butter in a heavy-bottomed saucepan over medium heat.
Add the mirepoix (onion, carrot, celery) and sauté until soft and translucent.
Stir in the garlic and cook briefly (about 30 seconds), without allowing it to brown.
Sprinkle in the flour and cook gently, stirring constantly, to form a blond roux (do not let it color).

instruction.title: Step 2 – Building the Soup
steps: Gradually whisk in the stock to avoid lumps.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until softened.
Stir in the tomato purée and mix well.
Add the bouquet garni, basil leaves, and ham/bacon skin (if using).

instruction.title: Step 3 – Simmering
steps: Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer for 25–30 minutes.
Remove the bouquet garni and ham/bacon skin.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Finishing
steps: Purée the soup using a hand blender, or pass it through a fine sieve for a smooth texture.
Return the soup to the pan, stir in the milk and cream, and reheat gently (do not boil).
Season to taste with salt and freshly ground black pepper.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Serving
steps: Serve hot, garnished with chopped parsley and croutons.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve hot, garnished with chopped parsley and croutons.
Accompany with toasted garlic bread or crusty bread.
Enjoy as an appetizer or a light meal.

chefTips: Do not allow the roux to brown; it should remain blond.
Gradually whisk in the stock to avoid lumps.
Pass the soup through a fine sieve for an extra smooth texture.
Do not boil after adding the milk and cream.
Use fresh basil for the best aroma and flavor.
